case_type_reason: Only spot values, ranges and peaks are printed. The MCA time series and the private medical conference records behind them are not public.
title: Documented CO2 symptom reports on the ISS and Shuttle with their CO2 levels

input_data.use: CO2 level as printed and the symptom outcome for each event

documented_outcome.quote: The crew noted that these symptoms subsided within minutes of reduction of ppCO2 to the 2 mm Hg range or when they breathed 100% O2 in an EMU suit.
It was assumed that installation of the LiOH in the interim alleviated the symptoms. There were no further reports after the CDRA was reactivated.
The EVA astronaut did not develop any symptoms of hypercapnia
Headaches at levels between 2.8-4.5 mmHg; worsening with increasing levels of CO2 accompanied by fatigue and malaise flushing.
documented_outcome.location: Background, Key Historical CO2 Concentrations, PDF page 4 (two-column layout), which cites NASA/TP-2010-216126

documented_outcome.quote: A retrospective analysis of the case reports found a total of 46 days with reported headaches and 1,670 days of non-reports (no headaches observed).
documented_outcome.location: CO2-Induced Headaches, PDF page 5 (aggregate from Law et al. 2014)

onset_relative_to_data: Same day as the printed CO2 level for STS-113; during excursions above 4 mm Hg for Expedition 6; months later (as a report) for STS-112.

expected_product_output.note: If the 7.5 mm Hg reading persisted over an hour the one-hour average is above 3 mm Hg; the paper prints a peak, so a test must state that assumption.
Above 4 mm Hg is above the 3 mm Hg one-hour limit; documented relief at about 2 mm Hg is the expected clearing of the warning by the rule, never by the assistant (rule 4).

expected_product_output.level: act on any hour averaging above 3 mm Hg, otherwise info; watch if the seven-day average is at or above 2.5 mm Hg
expected_product_output.note: Shows that headaches were reported near 2.7 mm Hg; the product must not tell the crew a headache is not CO2 because the reading is low (headache family limitation).

expected_product_output.level: none for the cabin rule; suit limits are separate (environment-hazards.json eva overlay)
expected_product_output.note: Negative control: no symptoms at a 3 mm Hg peak.

is_not: Not a dose-response dataset. The aggregate headache association (Law et al. 2014) is already the source of the 2.5 mm Hg watch value (C25); this case adds documented single events.

law2010.title: In-Flight Carbon Dioxide Exposures and Related Symptoms: Association, Susceptibility, and Operational Implications, NASA/TP-2010-216126, June 2010, Jennifer Law, Sharmi Watkins, David Alexander
law2010.url_read_note: Third-party copy of the NASA technical paper (30 pages; PDF metadata title 'CO2Technical Paper', marked Final, created 21 June 2010). NASA's own host (ston.jsc.nasa.gov/collections/TRS/_techrep/TP-2010-216126.pdf) did not respond on 2026-11-15 and NTRS returned no record for the report number. The NASA-hosted OCHMO-TB-004 cites this paper as its source for the symptom ranges.
